bibl.title: Constructivism versus Cognitive Load Theory: In Search for an Effective Mathematics Teaching

person.p: the tag layer; a sentence written by the tagger about the paper, always anchored to a quotation but not itself a quotation

span.label: critique
span.quote: I have presented the arguments and evidence from several researches that against the claim of Kirschner et al. (2006) about categorizing constructivist approaches into minimally guidance instruction.

span.label: constructivist instruction versus cognitive load in mathematics teaching
span.quote: Two major learning theories have dominated recent literature on optimizing knowledge acquisition: constructivism and cognitive load theory.

span.label: review
span.quote: The current study describes the elements of constructivism theory and their cognitive basis and show how they can be aligned with the structures that constitute human cognitive architecture.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: Scaffolding lowers cognitive load by structuring the task so learners attend only to the parts relevant to the learning goals, which is why constructivist teaching does not overload working memory
span.quote: These researchers argue that in constructivist approaches such as problem-based learning and inquiry learning, the teachers can provide scaffolding that decrease cognitive load by structuring a task that guide the learners to focus on aspects of the task that are relevant to the learning goals.

span.label: The author characterises the review of constructivist research as limited in scope.
span.quote: Even in this limited review of research on constructivist approaches, it is clear that the claim that “constructivist approaches do not work” is not well supported and in fact, there are supports for the alternative.

span.label: The empirical dispute rests on a prior question of naming: whether one label covers the other.
span.quote: I argue that some of these approaches, in particular constructivist, cannot be equated with minimally guided instruction

span.label: The contradicting result is about a different outcome from the one the original claim measured.
span.quote: Opposing this claim, Kuhn and Dean (2006) have found that direct instruction does not work so well for robust acquisition or for maintenance knowledge over time

span.label: The theory on the other side of the argument rests on a stated assumption about cognitive architecture.
span.quote: Cognitive load theory is based on the assumption that human cognitive architecture can only process a limited amount of information in working memory in a certain time

span.label: The paper argues from other people's studies rather than from evidence gathered for it.
span.quote: In the work presented here, I will discuss how constructivist approaches may provide instructional guidance and evidence that encourage the effectiveness of these pedagogical approaches and cannot be categorized as a minimally guided

span.label: constructivism vs minimally guided instruction - THE IDENTIFICATION THE WHOLE DISPUTE TURNS ON: one side treats constructivist teaching as an instance of minimally guided instruction and attacks it on that basis, and this author denies the equation, so both sides can be right about different classes of teaching
span.quote: I argue that some of these approaches, in particular constructivist, cannot be equated with minimally guided instruction

span.label: working memory and long-term memory - TWO DEFINITIONS, BOTH ATTRIBUTED: the first is the memory used for all conscious activities and the only one that can be monitored, the second a large and relatively permanent store, and both are given on the authority of named authors rather than argued for here
span.quote: Short-term or working memory is defined as the memory that is used for all conscious activities such as reading the text and it is the only memory that we can monitor (Sweller, 2004; Kirschner, 2002). The problem, especially in relating to instructional design, is that the capacity of working memory in saving information is limited. Miller (1994) in his research has found that working memory only can hold about five to nine items or elements of information that have not been previously learned or known, in a certain time. Long-term memory, in contrast, is defined as the repository that consists of large and relatively permanent store of information, knowledge and skills

span.label: scaffolding - DEFINED BY CITATION: the process by which a teacher or more knowledgeable peer alters the learning task so the learner can accomplish what would otherwise be out of reach, attributed to a specific author and year rather than stipulated
span.quote: The term scaffolding is defined by Reiser (2004) as the process by which the teacher or more knowledgeable peer assist a learner, altering the learning task so the learner can solve problems or accomplish tasks that would otherwise be out of reach

span.label: contradicts → Kirschner, Sweller and Clark (2006)
span.quote: In contrast to Kirschner et al’s point of view, I assert that the elements of constructivist approaches allow for flexible adaptation of guidance, making these instructional approaches more compatible with the manner in which our cognitive structures are organized.

span.label: builds-on → Hmelo-Silver, Duncan and Chinn (2007)
span.quote: In agreement with to Hmelo- Silver et al (2007), I argue that some of these approaches, in particular constructivist, cannot be equated with minimally guided instruction.

span.label: constructivism —distinct-from→ minimally guided instruction
span.quote: I argue that some of these approaches, in particular constructivist, cannot be equated with minimally guided instruction

span.label: cognitive load theory —operationalised-as→ working memory
span.quote: Cognitive load theory is based on the assumption that human cognitive architecture can only process a limited amount of information in working memory in a certain time

span.label: The paper argues constructivist approaches cannot be classed as minimally guided instruction because they allow flexible adaptation of guidance and so fit how cognitive structures are organised.
span.quote: In contrast to Kirschner et al’s point of view, I assert that the elements of constructivist approaches allow for flexible adaptation of guidance, making these instructional approaches more compatible with the manner in which our cognitive structures are organized.

span.label: Its concluding claim is that scaffolding is what makes constructivist approaches compatible with human cognitive architecture, because scaffolding reduces working memory load.
span.quote: The reason is that these constructivist approaches allow for flexible adaptation of guidance and reduce working memory load by giving scaffolding, so that these approaches are compatible with the manner in which our cognitive structures are organized.

span.label: Constructivist approaches such as problem-based and inquiry learning supply learners with scaffolding covering both how to do the task and why it should be done that way, so learners are not left to construct everything alone.
span.quote: In constructivist approaches such as problem-based learning and inquiry learning, students are provided with so-called scaffolding to support students’ learning of both how to do the task as well as why the task should be done that way (Hmelo-Silver, 2007).

span.label: Reviewing the evidence, the paper concludes the claim that constructivist approaches do not work is not well supported and that evidence points the other way.
span.quote: Even in this limited review of research on constructivist approaches, it is clear that the claim that “constructivist approaches do not work” is not well supported and in fact, there are supports for the alternative.

span.label: Realistic Mathematics Education is classified as a constructivist approach, and it differs from constructivism in being a theory of learning and instruction specific to mathematics rather than a general theory of learning.
span.quote: The constructivism theory is a theory of learning in general, while the realistic mathematics theory is a theory of learning and instruction specifically relating to mathematics.

span.label: The paper stops short of claiming constructivism is superior to direct instruction, accepting instead that working memory limits are real and both approaches have a place.
span.quote: I also do not claim that constructivist approaches are better than other instructional guidance such as direct

span.label: minimally guided instruction
span.quote: They define minimally guided instruction as “one in which learners, rather than being presented with essential information, must discover or construct essential information for themselves”

span.label: scaffolding
span.quote: The term scaffolding is defined by Reiser (2004) as the process by which the teacher or more knowledgeable peer assist a learner, altering the learning task so the learner can solve problems or accomplish tasks that would otherwise be out of reach.

span.label: short-term / working memory
span.quote: Short-term or working memory is defined as the memory that is used for all conscious activities such as reading the text and it is the only memory that we can monitor (Sweller, 2004; Kirschner, 2002).

span.label: long-term memory
span.quote: Long-term memory, in contrast, is defined as the repository that consists of large and relatively permanent store of information, knowledge and skills (Sweller, 2004; Kirschner, 2002).

span.label: cognitive load theory
span.quote: Cognitive load theory is based on the assumption that human cognitive architecture can only process a limited amount of information in working memory in a certain time (Kirschner, 2002).

span.label: intrinsic cognitive load
span.quote: Intrinsic cognitive load takes place in the mind of learners when the elements of the to-be-learned material are highly interconnected (Kirschner, 2002).

span.label: extraneous cognitive load
span.quote: the extraneous cognitive load is imposed by conventional instruction in which the limitation of working memory is rarely taken into account (Kirschner, 2002).

span.label: germane cognitive load
span.quote: The germane cognitive load is defined as the amount of resources devoted to foster the learning process.

span.label: constructivist theory (its essence)
span.quote: The essence of constructivist theory is the idea that knowledge is not transmitted directly from one knower to another or from teacher to the students.

span.label: five to nine items — Working memory capacity for not-previously-learned information, the limit the paper reasons from (attributed to Miller, 1994)
span.quote: Miller (1994) in his research has found that working memory only can hold about five to nine items or elements of information that have not been previously learned or known, in a certain time.

p.note: The full text of this article is not redistributable, so it is not included here. Every tag above carries the exact sentence it was made from, quoted under fair quotation. The article itself is at https://doi.org/10.48550/arxiv.2108.04796.
